newsitem.title: USA: ITT Corp. urges shareholder support.
newsitem.headline: ITT Corp. urges shareholder support.

text.p: Hotel and casino giant ITT Corp., fighting a $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid by Hilton Hotels Corp., is urging investors to stick with the company despite past disappointing stock performance.
In a letter to shareholders in the company's annual report, Chairman Rand Araskog said ITT is set to increase shareholder value by focusing on its core businesses.
"We are keeping to our long-range plan, but we are accelerating our short-term actions in response to the marketplace," Araskog wrote, saying 1996 was a transition year for the company.
The letter, released by ITT on Tuesday, did not mention Hilton's offer. The annual report will be mailed to shareholders on Wednesday.
"It is your board's conviction -- and mine -- that ITT management is best equipped to accomplish the task of creating shareholder value -- both short and long term," Araskog wrote.
Hilton is seeking to replace ITT's board at the company's as-yet-unscheduled 1997 annual shareholders meeting.

Investors had seen ITT's stock decline sharply in recent months due to competition and construction problems associated with an aggressive spending plan for its casino business. The stock traded at about $65 per share in June, but had eroded to about $42.50 when Hilton made its offer in January.
Hilton's bid values the company at about $55 per share.
ITT has rejected the offer and in February announced plans to focus on the hotel and gambling business and consider the sale of non-core assets.
Since then, it has sold its stake in French telecommunications firm Alcatel Alsthom.

It also has announced plans to sell its 50 percent ownership of New York's famed Madison Square Garden arena and the New York Knicks basketball and Rangers hockey professional sports teams, to partner Cablevision Systems Corp. for $650 million.

ITT has not announced what it will do with the proceeds of the asset sales, but most Wall Street analysts expect the company to offer shareholders a special dividend or launch a stock buyback in order to prop up the stock price.
In the letter, Araskog stressed actions to expand the hotel business, noting ITT recently was selected over Hilton to build and manage a 1,200-room hotel and conference center in San Antonio, Texas.
Araskog also said gambling performance was poised to improve due to projects at its Caesars properties in Las Vegas and Atlantic City.

Shares of ITT were trading at $58.75, down 12.5 cents, on Tuesday afternoon on the New York Stock Exchange. The stock has held above the Hilton bid price on views Hilton would have to raise the offer if it wants to acquire ITT.
Separately Tuesday, Canadian Airlines International announced it had added ITT Sheraton hotels to the airline's frequent flyer program.
